newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Motorola sees fast-paced growth in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees fast-paced growth in Brazil.

text.p: Wireless communications systems manufacturer Motorola Inc announced plans to launch its full range of paging products in Brazil, the world's fastest-growing pager market.

Larry Conlee, Motorola Vice President of Advanced Messaging Systems, said growth prospects in Brazil were huge as the market, albeit relatively small at a current 800,000 units, was growing at a rate of 100 percent a year.
"Most of the other countries in Latin America are only growing at a rate of 80 percent a year," Conless said in a news conference.
He said market penetration in Brazil was of around one percent against levels of up to 35 percent in comparable markets such as Singapore.
Conlee said demand for paging systems in Brazil was particularly high because of the local telephone operators's inability to satisfy demand for both cellular and conventional telephone systems.
He said he expected paging systems to be a cheap and viable communications solution for millions of Brazilians who would not choose or could not afford a cellular phone system.
"We believe paging will be a driving force in the wireless communications arena. Paging is an answer for the mass market," he said.
Brazil's telecommunications network is a virtual monopoly of state phone company Telebras and its regional subsidiaries.
The Brazilian government, which is in the process of defining its telecom privatization strategy, has said it intends to complete the sell-off of the state telephone network before the end of 1997.

Conlee said Motorola had received guarantees that the government would publish regulation for advanced two-way pager systems, which allow users to receive taped voice messages on their paging machines, by the second half of 1997.

Earlier this year Motorola set up an assembly plant in the municipality of Jaguariuna, outside the city of Sao Paulo, where it has already begun manufacturing cellular phone systems. Motorola do Brasil president Flavio Grynszpan said the company's objective was to build a multi-purpose manufacturing complex where the company would produce a full range of wireless communications products.
